sessions.phase_label: Word template assessment and requirement definition
Initial Word template implementation and review
Customer feedback corrections and document-by-document validation
Final Word template feedback and PowerPoint planning

requirements.title: Modern Word for Windows Compatibility
requirements.definition: The Word templates must operate reliably in current Microsoft Word versions on Windows PCs under ordinary multi-user editing.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the supported Word runtime environment; visual consistency across different users and machines is tracked separately.

requirements.title: Danish Template Language Configuration
requirements.definition: The templates must preserve Danish-facing content and use the client-confirmed default-language and style-language configuration.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers document and Word language settings; individual field-label wording remains an attribute of the field-label Requirement.

requirements.title: Shared Master Template Foundation
requirements.definition: A master template containing the shared styles and structural definitions must serve as the basis for the derived Word templates.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the shared master-template architecture, not the individual style values or document-specific structures.

requirements.title: Legacy Content Copy-Paste Stability
requirements.definition: Content transferred from legacy PBU templates into the new templates must retain stable, predictable formatting through a defined migration workflow.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the content-migration workflow and resulting formatting stability; table geometry and text-entry behavior have separate acceptance criteria.

requirements.title: Consistent New Style System
requirements.definition: The specified new Word style system must be present and applied consistently across every applicable template.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers completeness and consistent application of the style catalog; naming, typography, spacing, colors, and list behavior remain independently configurable Requirements.

requirements.title: PBU Style Naming
requirements.definition: Applicable active styles should use the PBU-prefixed naming convention when required for reliable template use and content transfer.
requirements.boundary_note: Style names can change independently of style formatting and behavior; the initial brief makes implementation conditional on its relevance to copy-paste stability.

requirements.title: Template Style Typography
requirements.definition: Named template styles must use their specified font families, sizes, emphasis, and caption typography.
requirements.boundary_note: Title size, Heading 3 emphasis, and caption typography are attributes of the shared typography mechanism rather than separate lifecycle units.

requirements.title: Style and Content Spacing
requirements.definition: Styles and structured content must use readable, consistent spacing that avoids crowding and supports required page fit.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers configured spacing around styles, rows, columns, and nearby rules; hard-return line spacing is independently testable and tracked separately.

requirements.title: Controlled Theme Color Palette
requirements.definition: The templates must include the required theme colors while excluding inappropriate extra color choices.
requirements.boundary_note: Color availability can be modified independently of typography, spacing, and bullet geometry.

requirements.title: Bullet Visual Formatting
requirements.definition: Graphic bullets must match the approved design, scale proportionally with text, remain vertically centered, and include the required level-specific variants.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers bullet appearance, including the green level-four variant; indentation and numbering alignment are separate behaviors.

requirements.title: Tab-Driven List Hierarchy
requirements.definition: Users must be able to use Tab to move applicable lists through orderly, consistently aligned sub-levels without the list breaking.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers level transitions and hierarchy alignment caused by Tab; visual bullet design and multi-digit numbering have distinct trajectories.

requirements.title: Numbered List Alignment
requirements.definition: Numbered lists must preserve consistent alignment when numbering grows to multiple digits and across list levels.
requirements.boundary_note: The failure beginning at item 10 can be fixed and verified independently of Tab-based hierarchy and bullet appearance.

requirements.title: List Continuation on Enter
requirements.definition: Pressing Enter in applicable structured list fields must create the expected next bullet or numbered item.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers creation of the next list item; ordinary multiline text entry that should not create a list item is tracked separately.

requirements.title: Table and Column Layout Integrity
requirements.definition: Pasting or entering content must not damage table layouts, prevent text wrapping, or push columns beyond the page margins.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers table and column geometry under content growth; reusable master-table component behavior and Board Meeting row insertion are separate.

requirements.title: Master Template Table Components
requirements.definition: Reusable table elements in the master template must function predictably without breaking or duplicating user content.
requirements.boundary_note: This covers operation of reusable master-table elements, not merely their visual style or the geometry of pasted tables.

requirements.title: Multiline Text Entry
requirements.definition: Applicable text areas and fields must accept ordinary Enter-based multiline input, including specifically requested headline and document sections.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers whether Enter is accepted for multiline text; the resulting line spacing and list-item continuation are independently testable.

requirements.title: Continuous Text Line Spacing
requirements.definition: Hard returns in continuous text must produce appropriate line spacing rather than the larger spacing intended between list items.
requirements.boundary_note: This is the paragraph-formatting result of a line break, distinct from whether a field permits Enter at all.

requirements.title: Fixed Layout Margins
requirements.definition: Bounded content areas must preserve fixed margins so text growth does not collapse spacing or clip adjacent graphical elements.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers fixed content boundaries and clipping prevention; table-column movement is owned by the table-layout Requirement.

requirements.title: Page Numbering from Page Two
requirements.definition: The first page must omit its footer page number, with visible numbering beginning on the second page.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independently configurable pagination rule rather than a general layout attribute.

requirements.title: Consistent Rendering Across Users
requirements.definition: Template formatting must render consistently for different users rather than changing according to local editing behavior or environment.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers observable cross-user rendering consistency; the supported Word platform and individual list mechanics remain separate.

requirements.title: Robust Standard Text Placeholders
requirements.definition: Ordinary fill-in prompts should use robust, easily editable placeholder text rather than inappropriate password-dependent legacy controls.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the underlying mechanism for ordinary fill-in prompts; dropdowns, checklists, and date selectors are retained as independent specialized controls.

requirements.title: Placeholder Clear on Activation
requirements.definition: Activating an applicable fill-in field must automatically remove its placeholder so the user can immediately begin typing.
requirements.boundary_note: Clear-on-activation has its own repeated failure trajectory and is separate from field labels, formatting, and control type.

requirements.title: Interactive Field Help Labels
requirements.definition: Interactive fields must have appropriate Danish help labels matching their intended placeholder text and preserving the field's purpose after content is replaced.
requirements.boundary_note: Label wording, matching, and persistent hover help are attributes of one help-label mechanism; automatic placeholder clearing is separate.

requirements.title: Visible Fillable Field Cues
requirements.definition: Areas requiring user input must remain visually identifiable without relying on unsuitable legacy-field behavior.
requirements.boundary_note: Grey presentation is a possible cue rather than the Requirement itself; control technology and field interaction behavior are tracked separately.

requirements.title: Interactive Field Formatting Stability
requirements.definition: Editing or replacing content in an interactive field must preserve the field's intended typography and formatting.
requirements.boundary_note: Formatting preservation can fail independently of activation, labels, and field-control selection.

requirements.title: Dropdown Control
requirements.definition: The applicable Board Meeting field must retain an appropriate dropdown control for controlled user selection.
requirements.boundary_note: The dropdown applies to a distinct document and can evolve independently of the Indstilling checklist and date controls.

requirements.title: Checklist Control
requirements.definition: The Indstilling template must retain an appropriate checklist or checkmark control.
requirements.boundary_note: The checklist has a separate document context and resizing limitation from the dropdown and ordinary text fields.

requirements.title: Reusable Date Selector
requirements.definition: Applicable templates must provide a calendar-style date selector with the client-confirmed display format.
requirements.boundary_note: Calendar selection and date formatting form one reusable mechanism; its scope across documents can change independently of other field types.

requirements.title: Board Meeting Field Alignment
requirements.definition: The Board Meeting 'Item and Title' field must align with the Topic, Proposal, and Start Time fields.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a document-specific alignment defect independent of row insertion and date controls.

requirements.title: Board Meeting Row Insertion Workflow
requirements.definition: Users must be able to add Board Meeting entries through the defined row-insertion and field-copy workflow without unintended borders or malformed rows.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the Board Meeting-specific row process and extra-border symptom; general table geometry and reusable master tables are separate.

requirements.title: Versioned Complete Template Package
requirements.definition: Delivered Word templates must be supplied as a complete package using the client-specified version suffix and folder or ZIP structure.
requirements.boundary_note: Version values such as v19, v24, and v25 are changing attributes of one delivery-packaging obligation.

requirements.title: Template Usage Guidance
requirements.definition: The customer must receive an explanation or walkthrough showing how to use the template tables and style-driven workflows correctly.
requirements.boundary_note: The guidance artifact remains independently useful even if the underlying templates function correctly; Loom is a proposed format rather than a separate Requirement.

requirements.title: Customer-Designed PowerPoint Template
requirements.definition: Create a PowerPoint template from scratch based on the customer-provided design and supplied graphical assets.
requirements.boundary_note: The confirmed deliverable is retained as one Requirement because the supplied history contains questions, but not final decisions, about backgrounds, logos, image masks, spacing, and dynamic bullet behavior.

unresolved_candidates.description: A proposal to prevent deletion of content-control fields is explained, but the client does not clearly accept or reject it; do not establish a field-protection Requirement without further evidence.

The client appears to accept an English default document language with Danish style names despite earlier requiring Danish as the default language; Event extraction should preserve the conflict and apply acceptance only if the local coreference is judged unambiguous.

The PowerPoint project is ultimately agreed, but several design questions in message 306 remain unanswered; additional PowerPoint Requirement atoms should be created only when the missing design evidence confirms those behaviors.
